title: Around town: rickshaws, taxis & the bus
goal: Flag down a taxi or rickshaw, agree the fare, tell the driver where to turn and where to drop you, get on and off buses, and ask how long and how far.
intro:
Getting around a Pashtun city is a negotiation. In Peshawar you'll haggle with a rickshaw driver, squeeze into a shared van or ride the BRT; in Kabul you'll wave down one of the yellow-and-white taxis or a shared car on a fixed route. Nobody uses street names — you steer by roundabouts, mosques and landmarks.

This unit gives you the driver-and-passenger Pashto for all of that. The grammar is the pairs of verbs that make it work — **کوز شه** 'get out' vs **ما کوز کړه** 'drop me', **ورسېږه** 'get there' vs **ما ورسوه** 'take me there' — and how to say **it takes half an hour**.

grammar.title: Doing vs happening: کول and کېدل pairs
grammar.body:
Many everyday verbs are a word + **کېدل** 'become' or + **کول** 'do'. With **کېدل** it is something *you* do or that happens to you (intransitive); with **کول** you do it *to someone or something* (transitive):

کوز **شه** 'get out, get off' — ما دلته کوز **کړه** 'drop me here' (lit. make me down)
سپور **شه** 'get in, get on' — ماشوم سپور **کړه** 'put the child in'
تاو **شه** 'turn' — موټر تاو **کړه** 'turn the car round'

Some pairs are single verbs in **-ېدل / -ول**: **رسېدل** 'to arrive' — **رسول** 'to get someone somewhere': ما هوايي ډګر ته **ورسوه** 'take me to the airport'. Likewise ودرېدل 'to stop' (دلته ودرېږه! 'stop here!').

**Forms.** Commands are perfective: شه / کړه, or و- for the single verbs (ورسوه). In the negative, مه splits the compound and takes the imperfective: کوز **مه** شه 'don't get off', or the one-word present: مه **کوزېږه**. The present of these compounds is one word: کوزېږم 'I'm getting off', سپرېږم 'I'm getting on'.

**In the past** the کېدل verbs agree with whoever moves (زه کوز **شوم** 'I got off'), while the کول verbs are ergative and agree with the person or thing moved: ډرېور **زه** کوز **کړم** 'the driver dropped me off' — کړم agrees with زه.

The trap: when the driver lets you off, it's کوز **کړه**; when you get off, it's کوز **شه** / کوز **شم**. ما کوز شه makes no sense.

grammar.title: It takes half an hour: وخت نيسي
grammar.body:
To say how long something takes, Pashto says the trip **takes (نيسي)** the time — نيول means 'to take, hold, catch':

**څومره وخت نيسي؟** 'how long does it take?' — نيم ساعت **نيسي** 'it takes half an hour'.

Many people say **لګي** 'is spent' instead, with the same meaning: څومره وخت لګي؟

**Counting forms.** After a number, masculine nouns like ساعت and کيلومتر take the counting ending **-ه**: يو ساعت, دوه **ساعته**, پنځه **کيلومتره**. Feminine nouns use their normal plural: لس **دقيقې**.

**In the past** نيول is transitive, so it agrees with the time taken (the object), with يې standing for 'it': دوه ساعته يې **ونيول** 'it took two hours' (m pl), لس دقيقې يې **ونيولې** 'it took ten minutes' (f pl).

**Distance.** څومره لرې دی؟ 'how far is it?' — لس کيلومتره لرې دی 'it's ten kilometres away'; for walking distance people give the time: پياده پنځه دقيقې لار ده 'it's five minutes' walk'.

**Fares.** 'How much to …?' is … ته **څو اخلې**؟ 'how much will you take?' (اخيستل). Your offer uses **درکوم** 'I give to you' — not ورکوم, which is 'I give to him'.

culture: Agree the fare **before** you get in — rickshaws in Peshawar and most taxis in Kabul have no meter, and a bit of good-humoured haggling is expected (start at about two thirds of the first price). Ride apps like inDrive (where you propose your own fare) and Careem are popular in Peshawar; the **BRT** ('Zu Peshawar') runs east–west across the city with a tap card. In Kabul, the yellow-and-white Corolla taxis go anywhere, while shared cars and vans run fixed routes and leave when they're full of **سورلۍ**. Address drivers as **کاکا** (older), **ماما** or **وروره** (younger) — never just 'driver'. Give directions by landmarks: a roundabout, a mosque, a hospital, 'behind the petrol station'. Women usually sit in the back of a taxi, and on buses and the BRT there are separate women's sections — men shouldn't sit there. For long trips, intercity minibuses and shared cars leave from the **اډه**; people bargain there too.

lessons.title: Getting a ride and agreeing the fare

tip.title: Haggling for a ride
tip.body:
- Agree the fare **before** you get in: … ته **څو اخلې**؟ 'how much (do you take) to …?'
- Too much? **ډېر دي** + your offer: دوه سوه **درکوم** 'I'll give *you* 200' — not ورکوم ('to him').
- Call an older driver **کاکا** 'uncle', a younger one **وروره** — and keep smiling.

lessons.title: Telling the driver where to go

tip.title: کوز شه or کوز کړه?
tip.body:
- **شه** (کېدل) when *you* do it: کوز **شه** 'get out', تاو **شه** 'turn', سپور **شه** 'get in'.
- **کړه** (کول) when you do it *to someone or something*: ما کوز **کړه** 'drop me', موټر تاو **کړه** 'turn the car'.
- رسېدل 'arrive' → **رسول** 'get someone there': ما بازار ته **ورسوه**.
- In the past, کول verbs agree with the person moved: ډرېور زه کوز **کړم**.

lessons.title: How long and how far

tip.title: It takes …: وخت نيسي
tip.body:
- **څومره وخت نيسي؟** 'how long does it take?' — شل دقيقې **نيسي**.
- After numbers: دوه **ساعته**، پنځه **کيلومتره** (masculine counting form) · لس **دقيقې**.
- Past: دوه ساعته يې **ونيول** (m) · لس دقيقې يې **ونيولې** (f).
- Distance: څومره لرې دی؟ — لس کيلومتره.

sentences.roman: kum bas pohantún ta dzi?
sentences.en: Which bus goes to the university?

sentences.native: په دې سټاپ کې کوز شو.
sentences.roman: pə de sṭāp ke kuz shu.
sentences.en: Let's get off at this stop.

sentences.native: ميټرو په شپه کې هم چلېږي؟
sentences.roman: meṭró pə shpa ke ham chaléẓi?
sentences.en: Does the metro run at night too?

sentences.native: هره ورځ تګ راتګ دوه ساعته نيسي.
sentences.roman: hára wradz tag rātág dwa sāʿáta nísi.
sentences.en: The commute takes two hours every day.

sentences.native: د دفتر تګ راتګ مې ډېر ستړی کوي.
sentences.roman: də daftár tag rātág me ḍer stə́ṛay kawí.
sentences.en: The commute to the office really wears me out.

sentences.native: ډرېور ډېر تېز چلوي!
sentences.roman: ḍrewár ḍer tez chalawí!
sentences.en: The driver drives so fast!

sentences.native: زه موټر چلول زده کوم.
sentences.roman: zə moṭár chalawə́l zdə kawə́m.
sentences.en: I'm learning to drive.

sentences.native: ته موټر چلولای شې؟
sentences.roman: tə moṭár chalawə́lāy she?
sentences.en: Can you drive?
